title: US is reviving shuttered nuclear plants to meet growing electricity demand and to power data centers
source_used: Associated Press, read as the ABC News wire copy
key_facts: The Department of Energy is lending as much as $4.4 billion to restart three shut nuclear plants: Palisades in Michigan, the Crane Clean Energy Center on Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island and Duane Arnold in Iowa, to restore a combined 2.25 gigawatts, roughly enough for 2 million homes and businesses (AP).
No commercial nuclear reactor is known to have resumed generating electricity after beginning the decommissioning process, though some have restarted after long outages (AP).

All three closed before their licences expired, largely because their power was considered too expensive; two now have contracts with Big Tech companies that pay a premium for carbon-free power for data centres (AP).

Palisades (operated 1971 to 2022, owner Holtec International) has a $1.5 billion loan approved in 2024; Holtec began loading fuel in August and paused after a fuel assembly tilted, and its power purchase agreements require it in service by March 2027 (AP).

Crane (Constellation Energy, 20-year agreement with Microsoft) hopes to be back online in 2027 with a $1 billion Energy Department loan; Duane Arnold (NextEra Energy, with Google) is targeted for early 2029 (AP).

Todd Allen of the University of Michigan says a restart is quicker and cheaper than a new large reactor; Edwin Lyman of the Union of Concerned Scientists says the money should address safety risks; Jack Spencer of the Heritage Foundation says there is no reason for federal money (AP).
NextEra's chief executive John Ketchum says none of the Duane Arnold costs are paid by Iowa residential customers because a data-centre customer signed a long-term contract (AP).
quote_evidence: The United States is making an unprecedented attempt to revive three shuttered nuclear plants to meet growing demand, especially from data centers The United States is making an unprecedented attempt to revive three shuttered nuclear plants to meet rising energy demand, including from large-scale data centers.

No commercial nuclear reactor is known to have resumed generating electricity after beginning the decommissioning process that takes one out of service, though some reactors have restarted after long outages.

The Department of Energy is lending as much as $4.4 billion to restart the Palisades Power Plant in Michigan, the Crane Clean Energy Center on Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island and the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa to restore a combined 2.25 gigawatts of electricity, which can power roughly 2 million homes and businesses.
why_it_matters_hint: Restarting closed reactors is a quicker route to carbon-free power for data centres than new reactors, but it has never been done, and taxpayer loans and safety upgrades are disputed.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (AP overview); loans and restarts are under way since 2024
notes: AP original (apnews.com, 403) read through ABC News' wire copy of the same text. The piece is an overview of restarts already under way; no new single decision is reported today. Not carried in earlier editions of this run.
